The analysis considers a 5-MW composite wind turbine blade made of T300/QY8911 material.
The maximum internal stress in the composite blade is 718 MPa, and the ultimate stress is 1548 MPa.
The fatigue life cycles N are calculated using the S-N curve model with parameters a = 1.816, b = 8.097, and m = 1.
The gamma process shape parameter v(t) and scale parameter u are used to model the stochastic fatigue damage accumulation.
The failure probability is calculated by integrating the gamma process probability density function from the critical fatigue damage to infinity.
The numerical results show the fatigue damage grows rapidly in the first 2 years, then increases gradually until around 90% damage.
The failure probability curves show a rapid increase as the fatigue damage approaches the critical level.
The proposed model can be used to determine optimal inspection and maintenance schedules to prevent structural failure.
Composite materials are used for wind turbine blades due to their better fatigue resistance and lighter weight compared to traditional materials like metals.
Offshore wind turbines operate in harsh marine environments with high-frequency and high-amplitude cyclic wind loads.
Monitoring-based fatigue damage prognosis is critical to prevent catastrophic failure of wind turbine blades.
The manufacturing cost of composite blades is about 15-20% of the total wind turbine production cost.
The design life of offshore wind turbines is usually 25-30 years.
Finite element analysis is used to accurately obtain the internal stresses in the composite blade under the wind loads.
The gamma process is proven to be more versatile and increasingly used in optimal maintenance strategies.
